title: A scheduler
description:
Simulate a priority scheduler with time slices.

```
threads: A (priority 8), B (8), C (4)
slices: A B A B A B ... (C waits while A and B are ready)
A blocks on I/O -> B B B
C runs only when A and B are both waiting
```
hints: `std::deque<T>` (from `<deque>`) is a sequence that is cheap to change at both ends, which makes it a natural queue: `push_back(x)` adds at the back, `front()` reads the oldest element, `pop_front()` removes it, and `empty()` says whether any are left.
`next` takes the front of the highest non-empty queue and, if it is still ready after its slice, puts it at the back (lesson 15.06).
A `std::map` sorted with `std::greater` keeps the highest priority first.
requirements: Ready threads are kept per priority; the highest priority with a ready thread runs next.
Threads of equal priority take turns (round robin).
Threads can block and become ready again at a given time.
stretch: Add a priority boost for threads that waited a long time, as Windows does.
